Criterion B1 (re-experiencing): MET — patient reports vivid memories and panic when reminded of the event. Criterion B2 (avoidance of thoughts): MET — patient actively avoids thoughts and feelings related to the trauma. Criterion B3 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient avoids places and conversations that remind them of the trauma. Criterion C1 (inability to recall details): UNCLEAR — patient describes occasional memory lapses but does not confirm consistent difficulty. Criterion C2 (negative beliefs): MET — patient expresses pervasive negative feelings about themselves and the world. Criterion C3 (blame): MET — patient frequently blames others for the trauma. Criterion C4 (negative emotional state): MET — patient reports constant feelings of fear and anger. Criterion C5 (diminished interest): MET — patient has lost interest in activities they once enjoyed. Criterion C6 (detachment): MET — patient feels detached from others. Criterion C7 (inability to feel positive emotions): MET — patient struggles to feel happiness or satisfaction. Criterion D1 (irritability): MET — patient reports increased irritability and anger outbursts. Criterion D2 (recklessness): MET — patient describes engaging in more reckless behavior. Criterion D3 (hypervigilance): MET — patient feels constantly on guard. Criterion D4 (startle response): MET — patient is more easily startled. Criterion D5 (concentration difficulties): MET — patient struggles to concentrate. Criterion D6 (sleep disturbances): MET — patient has difficulty sleeping. Total: Requires ≥1 criterion from A, B, C, D; found 14 clearly met, 1 unclear. Duration: met (symptoms started after the trauma and have persisted for more than a month).
